Which plugin provides the services every other plugin injects — read from the live Cordis

A settings section draws the graph, and a standalone page shows the same graph at full width.
Both r

ender the *same* panel: the two hosts differ only in what they can supply (a locale
service, a theme
, a window instead of a settings column).

## The two trees
There are two Cordis runtimes, and they get two graphs:
| | Host | Browser |

| Where it runs | the Node process | the page |
| Collected by | `collectGraph(ctx)` on the host | `

collectGraph(ctx.root)` in the page |
| Shown by | this section, fetched over HTTP | reported by the
page, read back by the viewer |

**They are never merged.** They are different runtimes with different plugins and different
service

names, so a merged graph would not be a bigger one — it would be a wrong one. The
Browser tab is a s
econd *source*, not a second set of nodes.

The browser tree cannot be collected by the Node half, so the page is the only thing that can
descri
be it: the section POSTs what it collected to `/dsh-plugin-dependency-graph/client`, and the viewer

GETs it back (one path, two methods). The report carries **the instant it was taken**, and the
viewe

r prints it — a graph a reader believes is current but is not is worse than one that admits
its age.

The browser tree's **descriptions** come from a route of their own
(`/dsh-plugin-dependency-graph/de

scriptions`), because the page cannot read `node_modules` while the packages
it is describing are th

e same ones: this half reads them and serves a name → description table.
That read is the one place

the two halves differ in capability, and it is why the merge lives in
`src/describe.ts` — pure, so b

oth halves run one implementation, while only the Node half touches
`node:fs`. Resolution tries the

plugin's own tree first, then bases learned from the host's
[该节后续省略]
## What a node reports
Selecting a node fills the detail card with everything the runtime knows about that plugin:

- **The package's own description**, read from its `package.json`. Absent rather than empty when
the

package does not say, or when nothing could read it — drawing no line is the truthful
rendering of

"this package does not describe itself".
- **Declared injections** — the services this entry's own p

atch row asks for, when it asks for any.
Read from the ENTRY rather than from the running fiber, whi

ch is why it sits beside **Injects**
instead of inside it: the two differ exactly when a declaration

went unmet, and an entry that
never loaded has no runtime injections at all. Absent rather than emp

ty: 3 entries of a 194-entry
composition declare anything, so a permanent "declares nothing" row wou

ld be a line about the
other 191. The rest of the entry's registration — mount path, group, `isolate

`, `intercept`,
`config` — is still collected and served by the JSON route; it simply earned no rows

.
- **Disabled** — a badge beside the state, on the entries that are switched off, and the state's
m

issing half: a disabled entry reads `not loaded`, exactly like one that is merely waiting, and in
th

at same composition all 29 of the former were the former.
- **Provides** — the services its fibers r

egistered.
- **Listens to** — the event names its fibers subscribed to, read from the dispatcher's o

wn table.
Listeners produce no edges: a listener waits for a name, not for a provider, so it is not

a
dependency, and drawing it as an edge would be a false one. The other direction is **Emits**,
whic

h the runtime cannot answer and the next bullet explains.
- **Emits** — the event names this plugin'

s own code sends, marked `seen` when the runtime was also
observed dispatching them. The only field

on the card that is not read from the running runtime,
because the runtime cannot answer it: the dis

patcher's table maps a name to its LISTENERS and never
records a publisher, and the one channel that

does carry an emitter (`internal/dispatch`'s
`thisArg`) is filled only for the explicit `emit(thisA

rg, name, …)` form — measured at 0 of the
[该节后续省略]
## What the graph reports
Two blocks sit under the drawing, and both are about work rather than about drawing:

- **Unresolved dependencies** — required services with no provider anywhere in this composition.
Onl

y *required* ones: an optional injection with no provider has simply not been offered yet,
and the p

lugin is working as designed.
- **Isolated services** — one service name with more than one live imp

lementation, i.e. provided
under more than one isolation label.
